This 2020 Toyota Highlander Hybrid XLE is presented as a midsize SUV with the equipment expected from the XLE trim and the added efficiency of Toyota's hybrid system. This model combines a gasoline-electric drivetrain with the practical packaging of a three-row utility vehicle, and its cabin is arranged to accommodate daily driving, family use, and longer trips without changing the basic character of the vehicle. This example includes a second row bench seat, which increases rear passenger capacity relative to captain's-chair arrangements, and the third row seat provides additional seating when needed. The interior is finished with leather seats, giving the cabin a more polished appearance than cloth-trimmed versions, while the overall design remains straightforward and functional.

This 2020 Toyota Highlander Hybrid XLE includes driver-assist and safety-related equipment that is commonly sought in this class. Adaptive Cruise Control is fitted, and Lane Keep Assist is part of the vehicle's equipment as well. Collision Warning is also included. These systems are integrated into the vehicle's broader electronic control and sensing package, and they operate alongside the rest of the Highlander's road-going hardware without changing the SUV's basic use case. This model's body style and hybrid powertrain are intended to cover a wide range of driving conditions, from commuting to highway travel, and the available assistance features add another layer of factory-installed technology to that role.

This 2020 Toyota Highlander Hybrid XLE also includes infotainment and connectivity items that expand its convenience features. Premium Audio w/Dynamic Navigation is fitted, bringing the upgraded sound system together with in-dash navigation capability in one factory package. Wi-Fi Hotspot is present as well, providing an onboard connectivity option for passengers and devices. These features sit within the center display and audio environment already built into the Highlander, and they are paired with the rest of the vehicle's controls in a familiar Toyota layout. The equipment list reflects a well-specified example rather than a modified one, and the technology content is consistent with a mid-grade trim that has been further optioned for added day-to-day usefulness.

This 2020 Toyota Highlander Hybrid XLE is also equipped with the All-Weather Floor Liner Package, which adds protective liners for the interior. The package is straightforward in purpose and is the kind of accessory set that is often added to help preserve the cabin from routine dirt, moisture, and debris. With the second row bench seat, leather upholstery, and the third row seat, the interior has the seating and trim items expected of a family-oriented SUV in this segment, while the hybrid system and factory options keep the vehicle's equipment list practical and complete. This example presents a combination of comfort, driver assistance, connectivity, and interior protection that can be verified by its listed features without needing any embellishment.

This is a 2024 Nissan Ariya Venture+ the range-maxed trim. Biggest battery Nissan offers (91kWh total / 87kWh usable), most efficient motor (238hp FWD), and everything non-essential stripped for range. EPA est. 304 miles.

THE HISTORY

One-owner, 54K miles, out of Victorville, CA. Lease return that went to auction almost exactly at the 2-year mark.

WARRANTY

Just over 2 years old, so there's still real time left on both factory warranties. 5yr/60,000-mile Powertrain coverage: about 3 years and roughly 6,000 miles left. 8yr/100,000-mile High-Voltage Battery warranty (covers both outright failure and excessive degradation): about 6 years and roughly 46,000 miles left. THE PLATFORM

Nissan's first ground-up EV architecture since the original Leaf and they took everything they learned from the Leaf's air-cooled battery and way overbuilt this one. The Ariya's pack is liquid-cooled, which means it consistently sees less degradation and less range swing from outside temperature than most EVs in its class, the Leaf included.

CHARGING, IN REAL NUMBERS

DC fast charging peaks at 130kW. Optimal charge window low-battery warning to 80% takes about 40 minutes and adds just over 200 miles (~5.25 mi/min). 0-100% on DC fast charging: just over an hour. Onboard Level 2 charger peaks at 7.2kW: a 0-100% charge takes about 14 hours, and a typical 10-12hr overnight charge adds 220-250 miles. Level 1 (standard wall outlet): just under 4 mi/hr.

INSIDE

Haptic touch controls built into the wood-look dash, one continuous smoked-glass display, and a genuinely good UI. ProPilot Assist Nissan's adaptive cruise and driver-assist suite is surprisingly competent and confidence-inspiring, not just a checkbox feature.

WHY THIS ONE

The Ariya is one of the best value EVs out there right now more interior space than most competitors, solid range, and a battery pack that (thanks to a decade of lessons from the Leaf) holds up better against heat and cold than most EVs in its class.

THE NUMBERS
